title: GPU-side delta checkpointing
paper_claim: Dirty-page discovery for mutable LLM state runs on the GPU and appends committed deltas to an AOF-style log.
repo_reality: The repo implements host-testable delta records, committed AOF replay, and an NVIDIA persistent-worker dirty-page scan used by Kimi Concordia.

title: NVIDIA persistent worker dispatch
paper_claim: A device-resident persistent kernel handles compute, checkpoint, append-log, and recovery tasks.
repo_reality: The persistent worker handles simple elementwise ops, dirty-page scans, AOF payload staging into host-mapped memory, and restore copies from host-mapped staging. The generic runtime can replay AOF records into a registered host region and refresh its checkpoint shadow, but durable AOF disk/file commit still routes through host-side code.
blockers: Durable AOF disk/file commit is still host-side after the worker stages payload bytes.
Generic GPU-side restore orchestration is still NVIDIA/Kimi-specific rather than a backend-neutral runtime task.

title: Kimi KV/cache checkpoint manifest
paper_claim: LLM KV/cache regions are registered with layout metadata so restore can replay the right deltas without relying on allocation order.
repo_reality: Kimi Concordia records region manifests, marks kernel-pointer regions as KV/cache, exposes an allocator metadata ABI for block-table and dirty-bitmap pointers, persists those hints in the manifest, snapshots block-table entries when available, uses registered dirty bitmaps in the NVIDIA Kimi checkpoint path, and translates restore offsets through old/new block-table snapshots.
blockers: BitNet/Kimi runners still need to call the allocator metadata ABI with real allocator pointers.
Logical-to-physical restore translation requires old and current block-table snapshots; without those snapshots the restore path intentionally falls back to physical AOF offsets.

title: NCCL boundary checkpoint and recovery
paper_claim: Concordia detects communicator failure, isolates a failed GPU, restores deltas, and reintegrates a replacement without full NCCL restart.
repo_reality: The NCCL shim exposes boundary hooks, MPI-aware AOF scoping, and a tested Concordia replacement-ring planner/state machine through a weak C ABI hook. Production communicator replacement and live failure orchestration are not implemented.
blockers: The NCCL shim logs/query-plans replacement rings but does not yet rewrite active rendezvous membership.
No live two-GPU failure/rejoin benchmark artifact.

title: SASS binary patching with live register capture
paper_claim: Binary-only kernels can be SASS-patched with safe-point trampolines and live register capture.
repo_reality: The repo has a Rust SASS-to-PTX lifter, diagnostics, PTX safe-point annotation, and a tested SASS live-register state-buffer layout ABI. It still does not patch binary SASS control flow or capture live registers on device.
blockers: No trampoline patcher for NVIDIA SASS control flow.
No device-side live-register capture stub wired to patched safe points.

title: Cross-architecture CTX migration
paper_claim: Instrumented state can lower through CTX and resume across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Tenstorrent targets.
repo_reality: The repo contains heterogeneous compiler paths, recovery helpers, PTX/SASS safe-point metadata, and a tested CTX resume-record ABI for NVIDIA PTX, AMD ROCm, Intel SPIR-V, and Tenstorrent TOSA targets. It does not yet lower live state into target-specific resume kernels or run a cross-architecture migration benchmark.
blockers: No target-specific CTX lowering and resume-kernel implementation.
